clue.text: Retiring surveyor rebuked and made redundant

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the surveyor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: CS stands for Chartered Surveyor
rebuked means told off sharply, rapped over the knuckles

explanation.surface: A surveyor stepping down was told off and then laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discarded as no longer needed has been made redundant.

clue.text: Fast-food outlet used by a carpenter

explanation.surface: A chip shop frequented by a joiner.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHIPPY is both a British fish-and-chip shop and slang for a carpenter; 'used by a' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British words: a fish-and-chip shop, and a woodworker who works with chips of timber.

clue.text: Turn in everything written on the computer

indicators.note: in means the turn's letters are placed inside the word for everything

parts.note: everything means all
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: A request to hand in all one's computer printouts.
explanation.definitionFit: An early programming language in which code was written for computers.

clue.text: An impresario may act pretentiously

explanation.surface: A theatrical producer behaving in a showy, affected way.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario may stage tunes, putting on melodies; the idiom also means behaving as if superior.

clue.text: Putting up braided hair is sweet

indicators.note: putting up in a down clue means lifting the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: hair that is braided is tressed

explanation.surface: Wearing one's plaited hair in an updo looks charming.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Putting up' turns TRESSED round to DESSERT; 'sweet' is the British word for a pudding course, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet is the British name for the pudding course of a meal.

clue.text: A hat used by Svengali

explanation.surface: A felt hat worn by a sinister hypnotist.
explanation.walkthrough: In George du Maurier's novel the hat took its name from the heroine whom Svengali controls.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with a dented crown; also the heroine of du Maurier's novel, mesmerised and exploited by Svengali.

clue.text: Swimmer comes out of a bistro utterly replete

indicators.note: comes out of means the answer emerges from a run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A diner staggers out of a bistro, completely full.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Joints of tender rib produced within the family

indicators.note: joints are cuts of meat, so the rib is carved up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Cuts of tender rib from a home-reared animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals mated with close relatives are bred within one family line.

clue.text: A large watch may be indicative of his success

definitions.text: A large watch may be indicative of his success

parts.words: A large watch may be indicative of his success
parts.note: a large watch is literally a big clock, and an expensive one shows that its wearer has made it to the top

explanation.surface: A chunky wristwatch is a status symbol for a successful man.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has reached the top of their profession is a success.

clue.text: Still he isn't unusually gifted

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of gifted arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Even so, he is not especially talented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'nevertheless', but it means motionless: the definition is someone who never keeps still.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person who cannot keep still is a squirmer.

clue.text: Want a little time

explanation.surface: Asking for just a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Want means lack or scarcity; split, the word is a brief age, a short period.

clue.text: Means to add note to Poulenc composition

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the composer's name is rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A way to add a note to a piece by the French composer Poulenc.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in the sense of wealth: riches and luxury.

clue.text: Highwayman takes money in N. Italian city

indicators.note: takes means the city holds the money inside it

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
P stands for penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: A robber of the road collects cash in a city in northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick TURPIN was a famous 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick of that name was a notorious English road robber of the 1730s.

clue.text: Question in debate the value of lawfulness?

explanation.surface: A debater querying how much legality is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedural query raised in a formal meeting; whimsically, the purpose or worth of keeping things lawful.

clue.text: New is but old Priest writ large." (Milton)

definitions.text: New is but old Priest writ large." (Milton)

parts.words: New is but old Priest writ large." (Milton)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Milton's sonnet on the Long Parliament: the missing word follows New, and is the church elder whose title derives from the same Greek as priest

explanation.surface: A line of Milton complaining that new church elders are just old priests in bigger letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue drops the blank: Milton's line reads 'New ___ is but old Priest writ large'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder of the Presbyterian church, a word that shortened over time into priest.

clue.text: Little likelihood of getting a substantial fortune

explanation.surface: There is not much hope of striking it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic idiom for no hope at all; read literally, a fat chance is a big opportunity or gamble's lucky lot.

clue.text: Handicapped member declares he can safely fail to vote

definitions.text: member declares he can safely fail to vote

explanation.surface: A disabled MP announces he may skip the division.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a 'pair' is an MP from the other side who also stays away, so an absent MP who says 'I'm paired' costs no vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicapped means damaged or weakened; the second reading is an MP saying he has an opponent's matching absence arranged.

clue.text: Married in mad desperation and took off

indicators.note: in means the married letter is placed within the rearranged word
mad signals the letters of desperation thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone married in a frenzy of despair and then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took off' looks like departing, but means mimicked; M goes inside IPERSONATED, the anagram of DESPERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them, playing their part.

clue.text: Capital I invested in building casino

indicators.note: invested in means the letter I is put inside the rearranged word
building means constructing, so the letters of casino are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: I put money into constructing a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts I inside NCOSIA, the anagram of CASINO made by 'building'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Create a popular outlet

parts.note: something popular is in
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: Design an outlet that everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something new is to bring it into being.

clue.text: Jewish teacher needs time to talk at length

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A rabbi requires time to deliver a long sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: To RABBIT (on) is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for chattering on and on.

clue.text: The material for a Scottish banker?

definitions.text: The material for a Scottish banker?

parts.words: The material for a Scottish banker?
parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, which has banks, so this is cloth named after a river on the Scottish border

explanation.surface: Asking what cloth a Scottish bank manager's suit is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river; the Tweed flows along the Scottish border and gives its name to the woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen fabric that shares its name with a Border river.

clue.text: Rational businessman gets money from property

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a man is referred to as he
rent is income received from letting property

explanation.surface: A sensible entrepreneur earns his income from letting houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rational argument is logical and hangs together clearly.

clue.text: Quick to criticise unconscious instincts

parts.note: to rap someone is to criticise them
the id is the part of the psyche holding unconscious instinctive drives

explanation.surface: Quick to condemn one's own unconscious urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and fast are synonyms for speedy.

clue.text: Wastes batter-coated food

explanation.surface: Throws away battered snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander time or money is to waste it; also pieces of fruit or meat fried in batter.

clue.text: Thieving youngster

explanation.surface: A thieving child.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper is old slang for a petty thief, one who nips (steals) things, and British informal for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a pickpocket, one given to thieving; and British informal for a small child.

clue.text: Loved making a theologian admit alternative point

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the theologian's letters take others inside

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
or introduces an alternative
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar was cherished for allowing another viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Loved and worshipped are close synonyms for cherished deeply.

clue.text: Dance wildly and break toe. Some find it amusing!

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of dance flung into a new order
break means the letters of toe are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone dances frantically, breaks a toe, and others laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes ANECD from DANCE and 'break' makes OTE from TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tale told for amusement, which some listeners enjoy.
